newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end flat, volume led by blue chip.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end flat, volume led by blue chip.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed barely moved due to a mismatch between buyers and sellers, but turnover rose sharply on foreign buying of a blue chip, brokers said.

The all share index closed 0.49 points higher at 728.81. Price gains led declines by 33 to 26. Ceylon Cold Stores rose 9.75 rupees to 120, Hayleys five rupees to 230. John Keells Holdings fell four rupees to 235, Development Finance three to 270.
"Trading is very difficult because buyers and sellers are holding on to different levels," said a broker who declined to be identified.
Turnover was 128.9 million rupees, led by foreign buying of 2.23 million shares of Lanka Ceramic.
Foreign buying amounted to 99.6 million rupees while selling was 9.9 million.
"The foreign buyer was probably attracted to Lanka Ceramic because at the current price of 40 rupees, the scrip is trading at just over nine times 1997/1998 earnings," said the broker.
